metadata.source_title: Evolution and Selection of Quantitative Traits

blocks.content: A key issue in selection theory is the expected time required for a given amount of allele-frequency change. Assuming that s and sh are small (i.e., there is weak selection, so that $ \overline{W} \simeq 1 $), we can ignore $ \overline{W} $ in Equation 5.1.c as a first-order approximation (see Example 5.1). Equation 5.1c then shows that the change in allele frequency p under weak selection is approximated by the differential equation $$ \frac{dp}{dt}=sp(1-p)[1+h(1-2p)] $$

For additive selection $ (h = 0) $, this has a simple solution of $$ p_{t}=\frac{p_{0}}{p_{0}+(1-p_{0})e^{-st}} $$ where $ p_t $ is the frequency of allele $ A $ at time $ t $. Often of greater interest is $ t_{p_t,p_0} $, the expected time required to move from initial frequency of $ p_0 $ to target value of $ p_t $. From Equation 5.3a, this is given by the integral $$ t_{p_{t},p_{0}}=\frac{1}{s}\int_{p_{0}}^{p_{t}}\frac{dx}{x(1-x)[1+h(1-2x)]} $$

Crow and Kimura (1970) presented explicit results for several important cases. If fitnesses are additive $ (h = 0) $ $$ t_{p_{t},p_{0}}\simeq\frac{1}{s}\ln\left(\frac{p_{t}\left(1-p_{0}\right)}{p_{0}\left(1-p_{t}\right)}\right) $$ whereas if A is recessive $ (h = -1) $ $$ t_{p_{t},p_{0}}\simeq\frac{1}{2s}\left[\ln\left(\frac{p_{t}\left(1-p_{0}\right)}{p_{0}\left(1-p_{t}\right)}\right)-\frac{1}{p_{t}}+\frac{1}{p_{0}}\right] $$ and finally, if A is dominant $ (h = 1) $ $$ t_{p_{t},p_{0}}\simeq\frac{1}{2s}\left[\ln\left(\frac{p_{t}\left(1-p_{0}\right)}{p_{0}\left(1-p_{t}\right)}\right)+\frac{1}{1-p_{t}}-\frac{1}{1-p_{0}}\right] $$
